summary: Light on the headland above St. Martins, NB: first lit 1835 on Thrum Cap, rebuilt on West Head after an 1881 fire, present tower dated 1966; still shown on the Coast Guard list.

light.fog_signal: horn: 3 s blast, 27 s silence (Coast Guard list)

structures.note: First tower, on Thrum Cap ledge; red and white horizontal stripes (LHF). Burned in the fire of 17 June 1881 that destroyed the station buildings.
West Head tower, 49 ft (15 m) to the vane, first shown 20 April 1883 (LHF). Its lantern room is on the St. Martins replica; the fate of the tower body is not stated.
Present tower on one corner of a concrete fog-signal building (LHF, 1966). Rowlett gives 1976 with a question mark. Coast Guard list: 11.7 m.

staffing.note: The keeper roster runs to 1987 (LHF). LHF does not say when the station was automated.

access.note: Reached from Route 111 toward St. Martins by West Quaco Road and Lighthouse Road. Grounds open, tower closed (LHF).

events.note: Octagonal tower on Thrum Cap ledge, with an attached dwelling (LHF).
A severe storm carried away part of the rock under the light and two boats (LHF).
Keeper Lamb was paid 10 pounds for assisting crews of vessels stranded near the light (LHF).
Tower raised twenty feet to forty-six feet (LHF).
Saxby Gale of October 1869 damaged the tower; repairs $298 (LHF).
November gale carried away part of the protection works; repairs $730 (LHF).
Fire from a defective flue on 17 June 1881 destroyed the station buildings (LHF). Temporary light on West Head from 9 July 1881.
New square pyramidal tower on West Head; white revolving light first shown 20 April 1883 (LHF).
Steam fog alarm in operation 1 September 1887 (LHF). An iron bell buoy had been moored off the headland in 1886.
Six-room wooden dwelling for the engineer, about 150 feet west of the station (LHF; Department report published 1907).
Present square tower on a concrete fog-signal building (LHF). Rowlett gives 1976 with a question mark.
Coast Guard demolished the fog-signal building around 2017, leaving the tower standing alone (Rowlett; 'around').

corrections.proposed: Present tower built 1966, 11.7 m; the 1835 tower burned in 1881
corrections.why: The 1835 tower on Thrum Cap was destroyed by fire in June 1881 (LHF). The standing tower dates from 1966 (LHF; Rowlett gives 1976 with a question mark). The Coast Guard list gives 11.7 m.
The Coast Guard list gives West Quaco at 45 19 25.3 N, 065 32 08.8 W, which LHF also gives. The OSM point is about 40 m away.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1835 date is the station's first light on Thrum Cap (LHF; Rowlett). The 1966 date is the present tower (LHF). Both are right for their own structure; the record keeps 1835 for the station.
Not settled. LHF gives 1966; Rowlett gives 1976 with a question mark. Recorded as 1966 with the dispute stated.

notes_for_editor: The 1835-1883 history (Thrum Cap, the 1841 and 1848 works, the 1869 and 1872 gales, the 1881 fire, the 1883 West Head tower and the keepers before 1884) rests on LighthouseFriends. LHF cites the Journal of the House of Assembly of New Brunswick and the Department's reports 'various years' without page numbers; none of that is in the corpus, so these are LHF's account, not checked. The keeper names from Brown (1884) onward are confirmed in the 1906 and 1907 keeper tables (Brown, Bradshaw). The 1906 tables show the station as 'Quaco West Head' and 'Quaco West End', and a separate 'Quaco Pier Light' that is not this station; keep these apart. Harry Bradshaw appears twice in LHF's list (fog alarm 1917-1948, keeper 1919-1948); not resolved. The 1908 notice 'Quaco lighthouse destroyed by storm' (source 6, scan p. 70, printed page not confirmed) is kept out of the events list and appears in the story only as an unresolved notice: the notice names no light; the same report describes work on the breakwater light at Quaco; Rowlett's separate Quaco Pier entry records a storm loss of that pier and light in 1908 (source 7), so the notice may refer to it. A human should look at the page image before anyone uses it. The LHF currency symbol is garbled in the cached text; read as pounds for 1834-1841 (1841 salary 'raised to 150'), and dollars after 1868. The present tower date is disputed (LHF 1966; Rowlett 1976 with a question mark). Rowlett says the fog-signal building was demolished around 2017, but the Coast Guard list still gives a fog horn; not resolved. Post-1960 keepers appear with years and role only, as LHF gives them. Fact-check of 2026-10-28: the 1906 keeper-table rows for Brown (Quaco West Head Light) and Bradshaw (Quaco West Head Fog Alarm) were matched to this station by OCR position (adjacent columns on scan p. 340); the 1907 'Quaco West End Light' row (scan p. 178) is also OCR-adjacent. The page images were not read: the in-app browser refused archive.org during this check, so a human should look at scan p. 340 and p. 178 before the keeper matches are relied on. The 1848 raise is stated as the source gives it (twenty feet, to forty-six feet). The 1883 contract to D.W. Clark is LHF's. The LHF pound sign is garbled, so the pound amounts are read as pounds, as before.
